edition.kicker: Primary-source tech intelligence, compiled from the live wire.

stories.title: Claude Haiku 5.5: Anthropic's cheapest, fastest small model - $0.10/$0.50 per M tokens, adjustable effort, vendor OSWorld 72.4%
stories.summary: Anthropic shipped Claude Haiku 5.5 across Claude, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure: ~$0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens for prompts up to 100k, which Anthropic says averages ~75% cheaper to run than Haiku 4.5. It is the first Haiku with an adjustable effort dial, and vendor scores include OSWorld 2.1 offline 72.4% (vs 15.7% for Haiku 4.5, 48.9% for GPT-6 Luna), Terminal-Bench 4.0 39.2%, and HLE 57.4% with tools. The same launch halves Sonnet 5.5 cache reads to $0.10/M, cutting typical agentic work ~20%. Caveat: benchmarks are vendor-run; a new tokenizer inflates per-task token counts, so the 75% claim is not a flat 90% list-price cut, and Haiku 5.5 is slower than Opus in Fast Mode.

source.name: Claude AI official X post (2026-10-07 18:01:16 UTC)

quality.note: Official vendor post plus official release page and system card; benchmarks vendor-reported.

stories.title: GPT-6 lands in ChatGPT for everyone with 'Intelligent UI': native interactive interfaces streamed in-chat
stories.summary: OpenAI is rolling GPT-6 into ChatGPT's main Chat tab: paid tiers get GPT-6 Sol today, Free and Go get GPT-6 Luna from Oct 8. The headline feature is Intelligent UI - the model composes answers from a native component library (text, graphics, charts, buttons, forms, small interactive tools) streamed through a compiler, choosing the format per question. OpenAI claims web-search-backed answers start 44% sooner than GPT-5.6 Instant on an internal eval. Caveat: Work and Codex routing are explicitly unchanged; this is a ChatGPT availability expansion of the GPT-6 family, not a new API model, and the speed figure is internal-eval only.

quality.note: Official vendor post plus official release page and system card; speed claim is an internal eval.

stories.title: Grok Bot can now search, read and monitor X
stories.summary: xAI's official account announced that Grok Bot - xAI's agent surface - can now search, read and monitor X natively. For builders, an agent that can observe the firehose where launches, outages and leaks surface first is a concrete monitoring primitive. Caveat: the post is terse with no API, scope or rate-limit detail, and the linked x.ai/bot page is the account bio pointer rather than documentation.

source.name: xAI bot official X post (2026-10-07 21:40:18 UTC)

quality.note: Official vendor account; feature-only announcement, no docs linked.

stories.title: Google ships Nano Banana 2.1 (gemini-nano-banana-2.1): GA image model at half the per-image price, Nano Banana 2 deprecated
stories.summary: Google released Nano Banana 2.1, its image generation and editing model based on Gemini 3.6 Flash, straight into general availability across the Gemini app, Search AI Mode, AI Studio, Flow, Stitch and the Gemini API (gemini-nano-banana-2.1). Output pricing halved to $0.0336 per 1K-image ($0.067 for Nano Banana 2), but input pricing tripled to $1.50/M tokens and the model thinks harder by default; third-party trackers rank it #5 on Arena's text-to-image board, behind OpenAI's GPT Image models. Nano Banana 2 is deprecated the same day with API shutdown on Oct 29. Caveat: Google announced from its main X account - no blog post, only a DeepMind model card - and the cheaper output assumes heavier reasoning tokens per image.

quality.note: Official vendor post plus official model card and API docs; pricing from third-party trackers citing Google docs.

stories.title: Robinhood executive says the firm bought about $25M of bitcoin; company has not confirmed, no filing cited
stories.summary: Robinhood's Johann Kerbrat told Starting Block at DAS Asia that Robinhood put roughly $25 million of BTC on the corporate balance sheet. CoinDesk reports the company has not confirmed the purchase and no filing is cited. For builders tracking balance-sheet adoption among US consumer platforms, an unconfirmed executive statement is early but weak evidence - it sits below the filing-grade disclosures that Metaplanet and MSTR provide. Caveat: Bitcoin Magazine's framing of 'first purchase ever' does not appear in the underlying CoinDesk piece, and a balance-sheet purchase can be sold without notice.

source.name: Bitcoin Magazine official X post (2026-10-07 10:59:48 UTC)

quality.note: Named executive statement via official media account plus outlet report; company unconfirmed, no filing.

stories.title: ChatGPT for Teens: under-18 accounts get the teen experience automatically, College Planner previewed for grades 10-12
stories.summary: OpenAI updated ChatGPT for Teens: under-18 accounts now get the teen experience automatically instead of opt-in, and it previewed a College Planner that gathers US four-year application requirements, deadlines, tasks and financial-aid steps, initially for grades 10-12, alongside new study tools. No model change was announced. Caveat: College Planner is 'coming soon', not shipping with this post, and the release is consumer-facing with little for builders beyond the auto-segmentation of minor accounts.

quality.note: Official vendor post plus official page; one component is explicitly a preview.

stories.title: SynthID Detector goes public: checks video, audio and images for Google-AI (and partner) watermarks, even after edits
stories.summary: Google DeepMind opened SynthID Detector to everyone: a public tool that checks whether content carries a SynthID watermark from Google AI or named partners (OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao; Apple listed as coming soon), including after edits such as filters, on images, audio and video. For builders, a free, cross-vendor watermark-verification endpoint is the missing piece for provenance pipelines - you can now verify watermarks without pulling in the generating model. Caveat: it only detects watermarks the partner systems applied, 'available to everyone' is Google's claim, and it tells you what is there, not who uploaded it.

source.name: Google DeepMind official X post (2026-10-07 14:03:41 UTC)

quality.note: Official vendor post with official product URL.

stories.title: Russia's Sberbank admitted to the first digital-depository register under 282-FZ: Bitcoin custody inside existing Sber apps
stories.summary: The Bank of Russia admitted Sberbank - the country's largest bank - to its new register of digital depositories under Federal Law 282-FZ, letting it custody bitcoin and smaller assets and move them through SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness with standard KYC, monitoring and reporting; a limited-customer rollout starts before a December 1 target. For builders, it is the first concrete on-ramp in Russia's supervised regime, following the CBR's register window that opened last week. Caveat: admission to the register is not a live retail launch, domestic crypto payments remain prohibited since 2022, and the Dec 1 date is the bank's own conditional target.

source.name: Bitcoin Magazine official X post (2026-10-07 14:00:15 UTC)

quality.note: Official media account post plus outlet article quoting the bank's statement; no direct CBR document linked yet.

stories.title: US government-labeled wallets move ~$100M in seized BTC and BNB toward Coinbase Prime; sale not confirmed
stories.summary: Arkham-labeled wallets linked to the US government moved 833.6 BTC (~$71.6M) that day - funds traced to the Potapenko/Turogin forfeitures and the Bitfinex hack seizure - into addresses that within hours appeared as Coinbase Prime deposit addresses, plus ~40,285 BNB (~$31.6M) from Alameda-seized assets. The Treasury/US Marshals chain still holds roughly $27.5B in seized crypto, and no agency has announced a sale. For builders watching the Strategic Reserve regime, repeated transfers to exchange deposit addresses are the tell to watch even when the March 2025 executive order says forfeited BTC is held in the reserve. Caveat: the labels are Arkham's, not a US Marshals statement, and a transfer is not a sale.

quality.note: Official newsroom account post plus detailed outlet article; labels come from Arkham, no agency statement.

stories.title: Wells Fargo in talks with Kraken's parent Payward for crypto trading liquidity
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports Wells Fargo is in talks with Payward - the parent of Kraken - to access crypto trading liquidity. If it lands, a Tier-1 US bank sourcing liquidity from a top-5 exchange house would be a concrete step beyond custody toward bank-level distribution of crypto exposure. Caveat: talks only, and the underlying scoop article is dated October 5 - the in-window item is the X post, not the article - so treat this as early-stage reporting.

quality.note: Official newsroom account post; underlying scoop dated Oct 5, talks not signed.

stories.title: Google Research: 3-month RCT with 133 patent attorneys - AI lifts drafting quality +0.38 SD, but skill retention is senior-only
stories.summary: Google Research published an NBER paper from a three-month randomized field experiment: 133 patent attorneys at 11 IP firms were randomized to early access to a then-unreleased Google Labs AI patent-writing assistant (now in Gemini Notebook). AI access raised unassisted drafting quality by 0.34 SD at day 10 and 0.38 SD at day 90; after the tool was removed, treated lawyers still beat controls by 0.32 SD on redlining - but that residual skill gain was concentrated in senior lawyers, while juniors split into more strong and more low scores. For teams embedding AI into expert workflows, it is among the first long-horizon causal data on whether assistance builds expertise or atrophies it. Caveat: one profession, one tool, blinded grading by domain experts; the blog posts the headline, the full numbers are in the NBER working paper.

source.name: Google Research official X post (2026-10-07 20:23:35 UTC)

quality.note: Official research-account post plus official blog page; underlying study is an NBER working paper.

stories.title: Stacks publishes the full PoX-5 / PoX-6 Bitcoin staking design: self-custody yield auction is the end state, ~12-month bootstrap now
stories.summary: Stacks Labs published the complete two-phase design for Bitcoin Staking: PoX-5, the whitelisted bootstrap that activated in the July 30 hard fork with the Endowment setting capacity, target yield and the fixed 5% BTC:STX ratio each six-month bonding period, running roughly twelve months; PoX-6 is the decentralized end state where any holder bonds BTC under their own custody, STX capacity is sold through blind auctions, and yield prices onchain. PoX-6 still needs a SIP vote and a hard fork, and auction rules are not written yet. For BTC DeFi builders, this is the first full parameterization of how self-custody BTC yield will actually behave. Caveat: it is a design explainer, not an activation; the reserve fund only accrues through PoX-5.

quality.note: Official project account plus official blog page with full phase parameters.

stories.title: Kazakhstan's central bank signs exploratory MOU with Tether on a tenge stablecoin and RWA tokenization
stories.summary: The National Bank of Kazakhstan, Tether and the Alatau City Authority signed an exploratory MOU to study a tenge-linked stablecoin and real-world-asset tokenization. It commits Kazakhstan to no coin issuance - this is the study phase - but it puts a G20-adjacent central bank into a Tether-stablecoin working group, a notable widening of Tether's sovereign partnerships. Caveat: the MOU is exploratory, CoinDesk's account does not link a government document, and stablecoin-plus-Bitcoin are separate tracks; the item is included under Bitcoin as central-bank infrastructure.

quality.note: Official newsroom account post plus outlet article; MOU is exploratory and no central-bank document is linked.

stories.title: Runway ships an MCP plugin: generate images and video inside ChatGPT Astra (also lists Claude, Grok Bot, Cursor)
stories.summary: Runway released runway.com/mcp: an MCP integration that generates images and video inside ChatGPT Astra from the same conversation, with its product page also listing Claude, Grok Bot and Cursor as supported surfaces. For builders, media models reachable through standard MCP means one tool interface across chat agents instead of per-vendor SDKs. Caveat: the launch post names no video model version and the post's own URL only appears in a same-minute reply post.

quality.note: Official vendor post plus official product page; model version unnamed.

stories.title: Eight Sleep publishes pregnancy/postpartum analysis: Pod users show smaller HR/HRV swings and more sleep in 3rd trimester and postpartum
stories.summary: Eight Sleep analyzed data from 100+ pregnancies and ~46,000 nights on the Pod, with a Research Square preprint (rs-10934514): third-trimester Pod members averaged ~3 bpm lower resting heart rate, ~2 ms higher HRV, and ~12 more minutes of sleep per night than published non-Pod benchmarks; postpartum, ~3 bpm lower RHR, ~16 ms higher HRV and ~15 more minutes of sleep. For the recovery/chronobiology builder, it is one of the first nightly-resolution wearables analyses of the pregnancy/postpartum axis, including new metrics like sleep temperature preference and REM. Caveat: it is retrospective and observational with no non-Pod control group - comparisons are against published averages from other wearables - and it is company-authored, not a geroscience trial; the X post's 'up to 16 extra hours' is cumulative across the window, not per night.

source.name: Eight Sleep official X post (2026-10-07 16:24:34 UTC)

quality.note: Official account post plus company blog and preprint; observational, no control group; blog date-only (Oct 5), noon US Pacific per limitation.

stories.title: IROS 2026 in Pittsburgh: 10 Best Paper/Best Student Paper finalists from 1,933 papers; South Korea takes 40% of the shortlist
stories.summary: IROS 2026's program in Pittsburgh ran 1,933 papers; ten made the shared Best Paper/Best Student Paper shortlist, with South Korea placing four - DGIST, POSTECH, KOREATECH and a 42dot/Seoul National/Samsung Research team - against about 6% of the program, while mainland China had three, the US two and Germany one. Per reports from the Sept 30 awards lunch, DGIST's LT-Mem (volatility-aware spatio-temporal memory for lifelong scene understanding) took Best Paper and UPenn quadrotor-formation work took Best Student Paper. For embodied-AI builders, the finalist set is a clean read on where the field's top engineering is going: VLA distillation for on-robot chips, quadruped parkour with depth-denoising world models, and non-contact manipulation of soft tissue. Caveat: this is a secondary analysis of the official IEEE paper index; the award decisions themselves were made at the conference's awards lunch.

quality.note: Outlet analysis cross-checked against the official IROS awards page; page date-only, timestamped at noon US Eastern per limitation.

stories.title: Evipedia's 870+ longevity evidence reviews land on Hugging Face under CC4 with daily refresh
stories.summary: The Lifespan Research Institute / Forever Healthy pushed Evipedia - 870+ evidence reviews of health and longevity interventions covering whole-body therapies, peptides, diets, blood therapies and more - to Hugging Face as a full-dataset, daily-refreshed release: one row per review with all metadata and full Markdown, CC4-licensed and built on their open-source AI4L 'Audit-Driven Prompting' framework. For longevity-stack builders, this is the most structured machine-readable longevity-evidence corpus available: a drop-in dataset for RAG pipelines, intervention triage agents, or benchmarking claim quality. Caveat: it is a curated review corpus, not primary trial data - the reviews' own evidence grading is the load-bearing layer, and it is a continuously updated moving target.

quality.note: Official institute press release with dataset details; page date-only, noon US Eastern per limitation.

stories.title: CASIA's Peiyan Li co-authors two IROS 2026 VLA papers (HCoT-VLA, StaKe) alongside BridgeVLA and SpatialVAM
stories.summary: CASIA PhD candidate Peiyan Li co-authored two VLA (vision-language-action) papers accepted to IROS 2026 - HCoT-VLA and StaKe - on top of his BridgeVLA and SpatialVAM work, per RobotToday. It is a data point that China's top research institutes are shipping a dense volume of embodied-AI control work into the main robotics conference pipeline, rather than only model launches. Caveat: it is a person/paper-roundup piece, not a single result with published metrics; the papers' full technical content is on the IROS program, not in the roundup.

quality.note: Outlet roundup; underlying papers in the IROS 2026 program. Page date-only, noon US Eastern per limitation.

stories.title: Hemostemix wins Bahamas National Longevity Board approval for commercial Phase 1 VesCell trial, plans dedicated longevity protocol
stories.summary: Hemostemix (TSE: HEM) says it secured full approval - including ethics clearance - from The Bahamas' National Longevity and Regenerative Therapy Board to run a commercial Phase 1 study of its autologous vesicle therapy VesCell for angina, vascular dementia and pain, and is designing a second VesCell protocol explicitly targeting longevity, measuring cognition, left-ventricular ejection fraction and immune biomarkers. It also advanced a non-brokered private placement (up to $1M, C$380.5k tranche closed) and moved ACP-01 test batches into cleanroom production. For longevity-builders, a regulatory board named for longevity green-lighting a first-in-human-adjacent commercial Phase 1 is a small but concrete marker of the Bahamas longevity hub. Caveat: it is a micro-cap, pre-revenue company (negative equity, ongoing losses) and the reporting is a TipRanks auto-newsdesk summary of the company announcement - Phase 1 is early evidence, not a longevity intervention proven in humans.

quality.note: Auto-generated desk summary of a company announcement; no primary press-release URL linked; financials are company-reported.

stories.title: Aura Bio's 300-peptide screen: a natural product repairs sunburned skin after the damage is done; 40% less radiation dermatitis reported
stories.summary: Aura Bio co-founders discussed the company's 'Million Molecule Challenge': a screen of 300 peptides at multiple doses for lifespan extension and damage resilience, which surfaced a natural product that repairs sunburned skin post-exposure rather than preventing it - reported ~40% reduction in radiation dermatitis, doubled collagen/elastin production, and early human effects, with an mTOR-inhibitor peptide rising to the top. For longevity builders, post-exposure repair compounds are an under-explored category relative to prevention, and the screen's explicit inclusion of lifespan-decreasing peptides is a sound control practice. Caveat: this is a media recap of founders' discussion, not a paper - most reported figures (including the 20% lifespan extension in the underlying model work) are preclinical/animal, and no trial results are yet peer-reviewed.

source.name: BoxLife Magazine recap of Aura Bio screening work (2026-10-07)

quality.note: Secondary recap of founder discussion; animal/early-human evidence, not peer-reviewed. Page date-only, noon US Eastern per limitation.

stories.title: Catch-up: FMC3 Robotics, Vector Informatik and PEM Motion form embodied-AI data venture in Germany after Stuttgart MoU
stories.summary: FMC3 Robotics, Vector Informatik (industrial software) and PEM Motion signed an MoU - announced alongside the Humanoid Robots Summit 2026 in Stuttgart and now formalized in industry reporting - to build a standardized data infrastructure for industrial embodied AI, with a planned joint venture in Germany. For builders, a common data substrate for industrial robot fleets is the unglamorous layer that decides whether cross-embodiment manipulation models ever get out of the lab. Caveat: labeled Catch-up because the signature date was never publicly pinned and coverage ran Sept 15-Oct 2; it is an MoU with a JV 'intended', not a signed entity, and no dataset spec is public yet.

source.name: RobotToday briefing on the FMC3/Vector/PEM MoU (2026-10-02)

quality.note: Two independent industry outlets plus summit venue; no primary company press release located. Dates date-only, noon US Eastern per limitation.
